newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzanian insurer brands airline deal illegal.
newsitem.headline: Tanzanian insurer brands airline deal illegal.

text.p: Tanzania's state-owned National Insurance Corporation (NIC) on Friday described as "unlawful" a $1.13 million insurance deal between Air Tanzania Corporation (ATC) and a British-based company.

In a statement and full page advertisements in Dar es Salaam newspapers, NIC said the agreement between the airline and London-based brokerage firm, Norman, Butcher & Jones Group Ltd, was illegal because the company was not registered in Tanzania.
The statement was signed by managing director, Octavian Temu. It accused a former senior employee of acting unethically to broker the deal.

"Apart from the unethical aspect of this conduct, it is also unlawful for any insurer or brokers not registered in Tanzania to carry out insurance transactions in respect of insurance risks situated in Tanzania," the statement said.
NBJ chief executive Stephen Pritchard told Reuters he had no comment to make on the matter, which the company had put in the hands of lawyers Williamson and Horrocks.
A spokesman for the law firm said Williamson and Horrocks had been instructed by NBJ to carry out an investigation into certain matters involving business transacted by the broker.
NIC said it had instructed its lead broker, London-based Fenchurch Plc, to obtain renewal premium quotations for 1997 for ATC which totalled $1.073 million.

"For reasons and motives best known to themselves, ATC rejected that quotation on 31st December 1996 and have reportedly accepted and adopted a higher quotation of $1,139,450," the NIC statement said.
It said the higher quotation was obtained through a former NIC employee it named and who was retired "in the public interest by ministerial order in July 1993."
Asked to comment, ATC Managing Director, Dominic Rwehumbiza said he was unsure whether the insurance deal was illegal but stressed the airline crew and passengers were fully insured.
"I don't know whether it was illegal or not -- it was the (ATC) board's decision. We opted to go with NBJ (Norman, Butcher & Jones)," Rwehumbiza told Reuters.
He described as "fishy" NIC's discounted insurance offer for 1997 which followed six years of premiums whose annual cost averaged between $1.57 million and $1.63 million.
"It was a raw deal we were getting through NIC," he said.
Rwehumbiza said ATC advised NIC on December 24 to process cover through the new brokers -- advice which was refused.
"We (ATC) told NIC to put the insurance for ATC through NBJ Limited. They (NIC) had conducted business with ATC since the 1970s and regarded the airline as a valued customer."
